newsitem.title: LEBANON: Christian warlord gets third life sentence.
newsitem.headline: Christian warlord gets third life sentence.

text.p: A Beirut court sentenced former Christian militia chief Samir Geagea to death on Friday for the attempted murder of a government minister but immediately commuted the sentence to life imprisonment.

The court ruled that Geagea ordered the attempted car bomb assassination in 1991 of Michel al-Murr, a Greek Orthodox politician who was then defence minister and is currently interior minister and deputy prime minister.

The High Judicial Council, Lebanon's top court, issued its sentence despite pleas from some Christian leaders to delay it until after the visit to Lebanon by Pope John Paul who arrives in Beirut on Saturday.

Geagea is the only militia leader from the 1975-90 civil war to have faced trial and some Christians see the authorities' actions against him as indicative of a government bias against their minority community.
His lawyers have written an open letter to the pope saying he is being victimised because the authorities have not yet achieved sectarian reconciliation in Lebanon.
Murr narrowly escaped death in the car bomb attack that took place in a town square north of Beirut.
The life sentence Geagea received in the case was the third he has been handed by the Lebanese courts in a series of trials since his arrest in 1994.
He was detained after a bomb attack on a church north of Beirut which killed 11 worshippers, but was subsequently acquitted of that attack for lack of evidence.
However, the government then opened up other files on him and he has faced a series of trials since then, unlike other former militia leaders who have benefited from a civil war amnesty.

Geagea's lawyers have complained that he has been held in solitary confinement for three years in an underground cell virtually without contact with the outside world. They say his health is suffering.

Geagea has already been found guilty of the 1991 murders of Christian politician Dany Chamoun and his family and of the killing in the same year of Dr Antoine Zayek, a founder of the Lebanese Forces (LF) militia that Geagea headed. He is serving life sentences for both killings.

He is also awaiting trial in a fifth murder case, the 1987 murder of Sunni Moslem prime minister Rashid Karami who was killed when a remote-controlled bomb blew up a helicopter in which he was travelling.
